checked_sources: P. Ghosh and T. K. Samanta, Generalized atomic subspaces for operators in Hilbert spaces, Mathematica Bohemica 147 (2022), Theorem 3.4
correctness.rationale: Condition (I) in the published theorem says that for every \(f\), the unweighted coefficient sequence lies in the Hilbert direct sum; it does not state a uniform Bessel constant. Define the everywhere-defined linear analysis operator \(Uf=(\Lambda_jP_{W_j}f)_j\). Coordinatewise convergence plus boundedness of every coordinate operator shows that a convergent graph sequence has the claimed limit, so the closed graph theorem makes \(U\) bounded and supplies the uniform constant \(B_0=\|U\|^2\). Writing \(a_j=\|\Lambda_jP_{W_j}f\|^2\), the resolution identity gives \(\|f\|^2=\sum_j v_j a_j\). Cauchy-Schwarz yields \(\|f\|^4\le(\sum_j a_j)(\sum_j v_j^2a_j)\le B_0\|f\|^2\sum_jv_j^2a_j\), hence the lower bound \(1/B_0\). With \(M=\sup_jv_j\), \(v_j^2\le Mv_j\) gives the upper bound \(M\). The scalar one-atom and two-atom constructions attain or approach both constants and force \(MB_0\ge1\); an independent scalar calculation reproduced the advertised upper sharpness formula.

originality.rationale: The primary Theorem 3.4 contains a quantifier defect: its condition (I) allows the displayed constant \(A\) to depend on \(f\), while the proof immediately uses \(A\) as if it were uniform. The audited closed-graph argument repairs exactly that gap and then derives optimal frame bounds in terms of the intrinsic quantities \(B_0\) and \(M\). Related \(K\)-g-fusion and continuous g-atomic papers assume established Bessel/frame bounds rather than proving this pointwise-to-uniform repair with the same sharp constants. Targeted Resultary and web searches did not locate a prior correction or the \(1/B_0,M\) optimal universal bounds.
residual_risks: An unpublished erratum or later citation may have noticed the same quantifier issue without being indexed.

limitations: The optimality is universal relative to the summary parameters \(B_0\) and \(M\), not a claim that every instance has those exact optimal frame bounds.
